stories.headline: SK Hynix halts review of US IPO for Solidigm, citing market volatility and share-price slide

key_facts.fact: On Friday, Oct 23, 2026, SK Hynix said its US subsidiary Solidigm has halted its review of a pre-IPO fundraising round and a subsequent US IPO, citing capital market conditions and share price trends.
key_facts.excerpt: "We have decided to halt its review of a pre-IPO fundraising round and a subsequent IPO after taking into account overall capital market conditions," the South Korean chipmaker said.

key_facts.fact: The IPO had been under consideration to help fund a new US factory for Solidigm, a former Intel NAND flash and SSD business; people familiar with the plans had said it could raise $15 billion and value the unit at $150 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: People familiar with the now-suspended IPO plans had said that the share sale could have raised $15 billion and valued the unit at $150 billion.

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix said the decision does not reflect any change in Solidigm's growth prospects or investment needs, and that existing facilities cannot meet rising AI memory demand, so it will keep looking for other ways to finance US capacity.
key_facts.excerpt: AI 메모리 수요 대응을 위한 미국 내 증설과 성장을 위한 투자는 계속 필요하며, SK하이닉스는 적절한 투자 및 자금조달 방안을 모색해 주주가치를 높이겠습니다.

key_facts.fact: The move follows regulatory scrutiny: Financial Supervisory Service Governor Lee Chan-jin said this week regulators view Solidigm as subject to South Korea's duplicate-listing restrictions, tightened in July; SK Hynix said those rules were not the direct reason.
key_facts.excerpt: Lee Chan-jin, governor of the Financial Supervisory Service, said both the Financial Services Commission and his agency viewed Solidigm as subject to restrictions on duplicate listings. However, SK hynix said tighter government restrictions on duplicate listings were not the direct reason for its decision.

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix shares closed 4.4% higher on Friday after falling as much as 3% earlier in the session.
key_facts.excerpt: SK Hynix shares closed 4.4% higher after falling as much as 3% earlier in the session, as the chipmaker halted its review of potential pre-IPO fundraising and IPO options for U.S. subsidiary Solidigm.

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix shares had fallen more than 30% since the potential Solidigm IPO was reported in late September, versus a 20% decline in the KOSPI over the same period.
key_facts.excerpt: Shares in SK Hynix have fallen more than 30 per cent since the potential Solidigm IPO was reported in late September, compared with a 20 per cent decline in South Korea's benchmark KOSPI index over the same period.

key_facts.fact: Other AI-infrastructure listings have also been shelved, including the IPO of Nvidia-backed Australian firm Firmus and a Singapore REIT listing for Blackstone-backed AirTrunk.
key_facts.excerpt: Other deals that have been shelved include the IPO of Australia's Firmus, which is backed by Nvidia and a Singapore REIT listing for Blackstone-backed AirTrunk.

stories.headline: SK Telecom's SK Hyper seeks funding for 15GW Korean data center plan; first 5GW to cost $350B

key_facts.fact: SK Hyper, the AI data center unit of SK Telecom, is in talks with big tech firms and financial investors to fund a plan to build 15 gigawatts of data center capacity in South Korea by 2035, CEO Chung Suk-geun told Bloomberg Television.
key_facts.excerpt: The SK Group's fledgling data centre arm has begun discussions with potential partners to help finance a plan to build 15 gigawatts (GW) of data centre capacity in South Korea by 2035, said Chung Suk-geun, SK Hyper's chief executive officer.

key_facts.fact: The first 5GW phase alone would require about $350 billion including equipment; SK Hyper aims to secure its first external capital by end-2026 or early 2027, followed by more fundraising over three to four years, sharing costs with tenants and outside investors.
key_facts.excerpt: The first 5 GW phase alone would require US$350 billion including equipment, he told Bloomberg Television. The company aims to secure its first round of external capital by the end of 2026 or early 2027, followed by further fundraising over the next three to four years.

key_facts.fact: Chung said South Korea's data center market is currently about 1GW, so the initial 5GW is roughly five times the domestic market; SK Hyper is discussing with hyperscalers bringing AI inference hubs to Korea to serve Japan and Taiwan too.
key_facts.excerpt: "Korea's data center market is currently about 1GW in size," Chung said. ... "we are discussing with hyperscalers ways to bring inference hubs to Korea, and we also want to attract training computing infrastructure."

key_facts.fact: SK Hyper is developing a 900-megawatt project in Ulsan and a 100-megawatt data center with AWS; phased operations begin in 2029.
key_facts.excerpt: SK Hyper is currently developing a 900-megawatt project in Ulsan and is also working with Amazon Web Services (AWS) on a 100-megawatt data center project.

key_facts.fact: SK Telecom, which set up SK Hyper in July 2026, plans to invest 750 billion won (about $567 million) in the unit by 2030; Chung said the pace of investment will be adjusted to actual demand.
key_facts.excerpt: SK Telecom itself plans to invest 750 billion won (US$567 million) in SK Hyper by 2030. ... Chung said his company would adjust the pace of investment according to actual demand, rather than commit to the entire plan upfront.

stories.headline: US Treasury proposes wider curbs on US investment in Chinese chips, AI and supercomputing

key_facts.fact: On Oct 22, 2026, the US Treasury issued a proposed rule implementing the COINS Act (passed in the FY2026 NDAA) to update its Outbound Investment Security Program, covering semiconductors and microelectronics, AI, quantum, high-performance computing/supercomputing and hypersonics.
key_facts.excerpt: The COINS Act authorizes the Secretary to prescribe regulations with technical parameters for "prohibited technology" and "notifiable technology" in five technology sectors: semiconductor technologies and microelectronics; artificial intelligence systems; quantum information technologies; high-performance computing and supercomputing; and hypersonic systems.

key_facts.fact: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent added biotechnology to the proposed regulations, beyond the sectors listed in the law.
key_facts.excerpt: Accordingly, the Secretary has added biotechnology to the proposed regulations.

key_facts.fact: The proposed rule renames AI systems as 'super intelligence systems' and proposes a broad prohibition on US investment in their development in countries of concern, citing rapid advances there.
key_facts.excerpt: the rapid advances in super intelligence capabilities of countries of concern warrant a broad prohibition on U.S. person investment in that sector.

key_facts.fact: The rule would apply to investments exceeding $50,000 and excludes financial investments such as stock purchases.
key_facts.excerpt: The department's proposal would apply to investments exceeding $50,000 and excludes financial investments such as stock purchases.

key_facts.fact: The rule targets China, Russia, North Korea and other 'countries of concern'; written comments are due by Dec 7, 2026, before final regulations set an effective date.
key_facts.excerpt: On October 22, 2026, the Treasury Department issued a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) setting forth the proposed regulations that would implement Title VIII. The NPRM provides the public an opportunity to submit comments on the updated program with a submission deadline of December 7, 2026.

key_facts.fact: AP reported the rule cracks down on American high-tech investments in China, Russia, North Korea and other countries of concern, building on a program begun by a 2023 Biden executive order.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. Treasury Department proposed a rule Thursday to crack down on American high-tech investments such as supercomputing and artificial intelligence in China, Russia, North Korea and other "countries of concern."

stories.headline: Huang dismisses 2029 memory-glut fears as chip stocks slide; Western Digital revenue jumps 55%

key_facts.fact: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told CNBC on Oct 22, at GTC Berlin, that he does not expect a memory oversupply by 2029: 'One of the things that's really great about memory is that you can always use more of it.'
key_facts.excerpt: "One of the things that's really great about memory is that you can always use more of it," Huang told CNBC's Arjun Kharpal in a wide-ranging interview on the sidelines of the company's GTC Berlin conference.

key_facts.fact: Memory stocks had sold off after an Oct 15 South Korean column predicted a 'red ocean' of new supply in 2029, and after China's CXMT unveiled a new DRAM design architecture; asked about partnering with CXMT, Huang said 'We're open-minded.'
key_facts.excerpt: "We're open-minded," Huang said Thursday when asked about whether he plans to partner with CXMT and use its memory product.

key_facts.fact: Huang said US chip restrictions accelerated China's push to build its own semiconductor manufacturing, and that neocloud demand far exceeds the capital available to them.
key_facts.excerpt: "We have certainly accelerated China's efforts to build its own semiconductor manufacturing capabilities..." ... "The demand for capital far exceeds the capital actually available," but predicted, "This issue will ultimately be resolved."

key_facts.fact: On Oct 22 the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 6.72% to 10,731.98 and the Nasdaq fell 2.60%, after Lam Research flagged supply-chain constraints in its guidance.
key_facts.excerpt: At the US close on October 22, 2026, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) fell 6.72% to 10,731.98 and the Nasdaq fell 2.60% to 26,008.86.

key_facts.fact: Western Digital reported fiscal Q1 2027 revenue of $4.38 billion, up 55% year over year, with non-GAAP gross margin of 58.1% and a 17% dividend increase to $0.175 per share.
key_facts.excerpt: Revenue of $4.38 billion, up 55% year-over-year ... we are raising our quarterly cash dividend by 17% to $0.175 per share

key_facts.fact: Western Digital guided fiscal Q2 revenue to about $5.1 billion, up 66% to 72% year over year.
key_facts.excerpt: Q2FY27 revenue expected to be up 66% to 72% year-over-year ... we expect revenue of $5.1 billion, non-GAAP gross margin of 60.5%, and non-GAAP EPS of $5.80.

key_facts.fact: WD CEO Irving Tan said storage demand is spreading to neoclouds and AI frontier labs, and that its first HAMR drive is on track for volume shipments in the first half of 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: We are increasingly seeing storage demand grow beyond our core cloud and hyperscale customers into enterprise environments and into newer end markets such as neocloud and AI frontier labs ... are on schedule to begin volume shipments in the first half of calendar year 2027.

stories.headline: Brazilian-founded Tractian raises $130M Series D at $1.4B valuation for industrial physical AI

key_facts.fact: On Oct 22, 2026, Tractian announced a $130 million Series D led by Sapphire Ventures and co-led by M&G's Catalyst, valuing the company at $1.4 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Tractian, the leading Physical AI platform for asset-heavy industries, today announced a $130M Series D round led by Sapphire Ventures and co-led with M&G's Catalyst. The round values the company at $1.4 billion

key_facts.fact: Other investors include N47, General Catalyst, Bosch Ventures, 53 Stations, Monashees, Endeavor Catalyst, Norte Ventures and Y Combinator.
key_facts.excerpt: New and existing investors such as N47, General Catalyst, Bosch Ventures, 53 Stations, Monashees, Endeavor Catalyst, Norte Ventures, and Y Combinator also participated.

key_facts.fact: Tractian makes its own vibration, ultrasound and electrical sensors plus AI models (including JANUS) that diagnose machine failures; it plans to push into data centers, defense, energy infrastructure and Europe.
key_facts.excerpt: Proprietary hardware. A family of Tractian-designed sensors that capture a machine's mechanical, electrical and operational signals ... the company is pushing further into Europe and markets where failure is not an option, including data centers, defense and the public sector, and energy infrastructure.

key_facts.fact: The valuation is 94% above the $800 million of its Series C in November 2024, and annualized revenue passed $100 million in September 2026, up from $40 million in 2024.
key_facts.excerpt: O valuation é 94% maior que o de US$ 800 milhões registrado na Série C ... a receita anualizada ultrapassou os US$ 100 milhões em setembro deste ano, ante US$ 40 milhões em 2024.

key_facts.fact: Founded in 2019 by Igor Marinelli, Gabriel Lameirinhas and Leonardo Vieira, the originally Brazilian company is headquartered in Atlanta and has more than 700 employees and 2,000+ customers including Eli Lilly, Whirlpool, Coca-Cola and Embraer.
key_facts.excerpt: Fundada em 2019 por Igor Marinelli, Gabriel Lameirinhas e Leonardo Vieira, a empresa é originalmente brasileira, mas a principal sede do negócio está localizada em Atlanta (EUA). O negócio reúne mais de 700 funcionários.

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg Línea says Tractian is Latin America's second AI unicorn, after legaltech Enter (valued at $1.2 billion earlier this year).
key_facts.excerpt: Com o aporte, a Tractian se torna o segundo unicórnio de inteligência artificial da região. O primeiro foi a legaltech Enter, avaliada em US$ 1,2 bilhão no começo deste ano.

stories.headline: Robots-as-a-service firm Formic raises $50M to move into general-purpose factory robotics

key_facts.fact: Chicago-based Formic raised $50 million in growth capital on Oct 22, 2026, including a Series B led by Mercato Partners with Light Ray Ventures, Lightscape Partners and Citi, plus debt financing from S2G Investments.
key_facts.excerpt: The financing includes a Series B led by Mercato Partners, with participation from Light Ray Ventures, Lightscape Partners, Citi, and other new and existing investors, as well as debt financing from S2G Investments.

key_facts.fact: Axios reported the round as $50 million total, in an exclusive interview with CEO Saman Farid.
key_facts.excerpt: Formic, a physical AI commercialization platform, raised $50 million in financing, CEO Saman Farid tells Axios exclusively.

key_facts.fact: Formic rents robots to manufacturers for one monthly fee with no upfront capital, and operates hundreds of robots across 100+ facilities in 30+ states, with 99.6% fleet uptime and 97% customer renewal.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, Formic operates hundreds of robots across more than 100 facilities in over 30 states. Its fleet runs at 99.6% uptime, and 97% of customers renew.

key_facts.fact: The company has logged more than 750,000 hours of live production and will use the money to expand from task-specific automation into general-purpose robotics and new applications such as metal fabrication.
key_facts.excerpt: Series B led by Mercato Partners will accelerate the expansion into general-purpose robotics, building on more than 750,000 hours of live production across 100+ facilities.

key_facts.fact: Formic is working with Physical Intelligence to adapt that company's robotic foundation models using manufacturing data from Formic's deployed fleet.
key_facts.excerpt: Formic operates hundreds of robots across more than 100 facilities in more than 30 states and is working with Physical Intelligence to adapt robotic foundation models using manufacturing data from its deployed systems.
